en.title: Maximum Heart Rate Difference Within an Activity Level
en.description:
Each record contains a heart rate and an activity level. For each activity level, compute its maximum heart rate minus its minimum heart rate, and output the largest of these differences across all levels. A level with a single record has a difference of 0.

The standard input/output, examples, and tests are written by CSWork; ranges marked "this site" are judging conventions and are not claimed to be original interview limits.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..100000), followed by n lines, each with a heart rate (0..300) and a non-empty activity level identifier that contains no whitespace.
en.output: Output the answer as described; results for multiple queries are separated by spaces, in order.
en.explanation: Example 1: the Normal group has a maximum of 100 and a minimum of 87, a difference of 13; the other two groups each have only one record, with difference 0, so the output is 13. Example 2: heart rates 0 and 300 in the same group give a difference of 300. Example 3: the two records are not in the same group, so each group's difference is 0.
hints: Maintain the minimum and maximum heart rate for each level, then take the largest range.
